## Features [Permalink: Features](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#features) - [x] Search Ahmia.fi from the command line - [x] Export results to CSV - [x] Enable/Disable routing requests through Tor - [x] Return results in a clean readable format - [x] Response caching for faster repeated searches - [x] Configurable result limits and request timeout ## Installation [Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#installation) **PyAhmia** is available on PyPI and can be installed like so: ``` pip install pyahmia ``` This will install `ahmia` and `pyahmia` as commands. ## Usage [Permalink: Usage](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#usage) To start searching, you can call `ahmia` (or `pyahmia`) with the specified search query. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY ``` ### Routing Traffic Through Tor (Optional) [Permalink: Routing Traffic Through Tor (Optional)](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#routing-traffic-through-tor-optional) **PyAhmia works without Tor, but you can enable routing traffic through Tor if you want.** When this is enabled, it will use Ahmia's darknet url instead of the clearnet variant. To enable routing through Tor, you can call `ahmia` with the `-t, --use-tor` flag. This assumes the tor service is running in the background, otherwise, the command will fail before you can say "hidden wiki". If Tor is not installed, you can check out the installation scripts located in [pyahmia/scripts](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia/tree/master/scripts). _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --use-tor ``` ### Exporting Output [Permalink: Exporting Output](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#exporting-output) PyAhmia only supports exporting data to csv files (for now), and in order to export, you'll need to specify the `-e, --export` flag. This will export your search results to a file named after your search query. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --export ``` ### Filtering Results by Time Period [Permalink: Filtering Results by Time Period](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#filtering-results-by-time-period) Results can be filtered by 3 time periods (day, week, month). By default, results will be taken from all time periods ( all). You can change this by using the `-p, --period` option, and pass the time period you want to get results from. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --period week ``` ### Limiting Results [Permalink: Limiting Results](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#limiting-results) By default, PyAhmia displays up to 100 results. You can change this with the `-l, --limit` option. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --limit 50 ``` To show all results regardless of the limit, use the `-a, --all` flag. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --all ``` ### Caching [Permalink: Caching](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#caching) PyAhmia caches responses by default to reduce redundant requests. To disable caching, use the `--no-cache` flag. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --no-cache ``` ### Request Timeout [Permalink: Request Timeout](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#request-timeout) You can set a custom timeout (in seconds) for requests using the `--timeout` option. The default is 10 seconds. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --timeout 30 ``` ## In Conclusion [Permalink: In Conclusion](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#in-conclusion) Don't send too many requests with pyahmia. Be nice to the owners of Ahmia.fi :) ## Contributing [Permalink: Contributing](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#contributing) Contributions are welcome! If you’d like to improve PyAhmia, fix a bug, or add a feature: 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a new branch for your changes 3. Commit and push your changes 4. Open a pull request Please keep PRs focused and provide a clear description of the problem being solved. Bug reports and feature requests are also appreciated, just open an issue. ## License [Permalink: License](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#license) This project is licensed under the MIT License, see the [LICENSE](https://codeberg.org/rly0nheart/pyahmia/raw/branch/master/LICENSE) file for details.
